title: Best Influencer Marketing Experts (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire an influencer marketing expert: what the service should include, how to brief it, what drives the price and the red flags.
intro: Influencer marketing puts your product in front of an audience that already trusts someone. The risk is paying for followers who are not real, posts that are not labeled as ads, or creators whose audience does not match your customers. This guide helps you hire someone to find and manage the right creators.

faq.q: What does an influencer marketing expert actually do?
faq.a: Usually they plan the campaign, find suitable creators, contact them, negotiate terms, manage the content and report results. Some only deliver a list of creators. Check which parts are included.

faq.q: Are influencer fees included in the price?
faq.a: Usually not. The expert's fee covers their work; creators are paid separately, in money, free products or both. Agree on a separate budget for creators before outreach starts.

faq.q: Do posts have to be labeled as ads?
faq.a: In many countries, yes. Paid or gifted posts usually need a clear label such as #ad or the platform's paid partnership tag. Check the advertising rules where you and the creators are based.

faq.q: How can I spot fake followers?
faq.a: Look for sudden jumps in followers, very low engagement for the follower count, generic comments and an audience from countries the creator does not talk to. Ask the expert how they check this.

faq.q: What is the difference between influencer marketing and UGC?
faq.a: With influencer marketing, the creator posts to their own audience. With UGC, a creator makes videos for you to post or use in ads, and their audience does not matter. Many brands use both.
